transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SA), Amanda (Crestline Procurement), Ravi (Crestline Security), Nora (Crestline Finance), Tom (Crestline Legal)

Summary:
Quick procurement check focusing on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA acceptance criteria, pilot billing pathways (hosted vs dedicated pricing triggers), and KMS BYOK fallback plan. Customer emphasized data residency and auditability; wants clear acceptance criteria for pilot metrics and a single escalation contact.

Topics:
- MSA redline hotspots (indemnity, liability cap, data residency clause)
- DPA: controller/processor language, sub-processor list cadence
- SLA: P99 vs P95, credit calculation, incident communication timeline
- Pricing: pilot discounted commit, burst/dedicated pricing triggers, egress fees
- KMS: BYOK flow, HSM/KMS certifications, fallback to Redwood-managed keys
- Next steps: redlines, pilot SOW, technical runbook call

00:00 Jordan: okay hey everybody thanks for joining, um we'll go through the contract points and then the ops pieces, is that right Amanda?
00:14 Amanda: yeah thanks Jordan uh this is mostly to make sure procurement buys the path, um i have Nora on for billing nuance and Tom for legal stuff so we'll try to keep it tight.
00:28 Priya: quick note — we'll cover KMS and pilot acceptance after the commercial bits, and then Liam can walk the technical fallback.
00:40 Tom: great, i'll flag the big ones up front: liability cap, data residency, and audit logs — we need specific language not just a promise.
00:51 Jordan: got it, that's on our redline list. On liability cap we proposed standard SaaS cap at 12 months of fees — is that a hard stop?
01:05 Tom: that's our baseline, we might be able to flex for the pilot but enterprise needs a carve for willful misconduct, etc.
01:16 Nora: from finance: pilot pricing needs a clear conversion path — we can't be surprised by a big jump at production. We want a modeled estimate tied to token volumes.
01:29 Jordan: absolutely — we'll send a pricing worksheet. For pilot we typically do a month-to-month discounted rate and a conversion trigger if usage exceeds X tokens per month.
01:42 Nora: what is X? we need a concrete number to evaluate impact.
01:45 Priya: from Priya, based on similar customers we'd propose 200M tokens/month as the initial burst threshold, with a blended dedicated price after that but we can make the threshold lower if finance prefers.
01:58 Nora: 200M is large for us — can you do 75M?
02:02 Jordan: we can propose 75M as an option; it does change unit price. we'll reflect both scenarios in the worksheet.
02:12 Ravi: security question about encryption and keys — we require BYOK for EU data and need to understand fallback: if our key provider has an outage, can Redwood operate with Redwood-managed keys temporarily? what's the process and audit trail?
02:25 Priya: yes that's one of the standard flows — BYOK with a fallback to Redwood-managed keys under an emergency access policy. We'll document steps, timeline, and required approvals. The fallback is an off-normal path and we can require a signed emergency authorization.
02:40 Ravi: and the logs? we need proof of key rotation attempts and access logs stored for seven years.
02:46 Liam: we capture KMS audit logs and push a copy to your SIEM via syslog / cloud logging export; retention is configurable — for enterprise we can arrange longer retention via a retention add-on.
02:59 Ravi: certifications — do you have an HSM attestation and does your key flow support external HSMs?
03:06 Priya: we support external KMS endpoints (AWS KMS, GCP, Azure) and HSM-backed CMKs; we'll include the architecture diagram. For attestation we provide SOC 2 reports; for FIPS/HSM attestation we can share specifics under NDA.
03:20 Tom: DPA question: sub-processor list cadence, how often do you update it? our compliance team wants quarterly notice for new sub-processors.
03:29 Jordan: we publish a current sub-processor list online and provide notification of changes; quarterly notices are reasonable and we can add contract language.
03:36 Tom: perfect. on SLA: we need P99 latency and a concrete crediting formula. Your standard doc has P95.
03:46 Jordan: right, our hosted tier SLO is P95 for 2-second median latency for typical chat workloads; P99 is available as an add-on SLA for dedicated capacity. For hosted we can commit to a P99 percentile but it changes the revenue model.
03:59 Nora: can you give an example credit calc? we need to show to finance.
04:04 Priya: typical approach: credits start at 10% for missing monthly uptime of 99.9%, increasing stepwise; for latency SLOs there's a token-based credit per affected route. We'll send a simple table.
04:18 Amanda: egress fees — we were surprised in other pilots. do you charge egress separately for logs/exported artifacts?
04:26 Jordan: egress on larger exports (bulk log exports, egressed model outputs to third-party storage) can carry fees; typical API token usage is included. We'll model egress scenarios.
04:35 Amanda: we need the worst-case pro forma — egress plus KMS request pricing, please.
04:42 Liam: note: if you keep embeddings and vectors on our hosted storage vs exporting to your own S3, the egress delta changes. We'll call out the paths in the worksheet.
04:55 Tom: liability language again — indemnity for third-party IP must be explicit; we can share a short clause we'd like included.
05:03 Jordan: send the proposed clause to me and Tom we'll take it into our legal team, we usually accept reasonable IP carveouts.
05:10 Amanda: timeline — procurement needs approvals by 4/30 to start pilot 5/5. Is that realistic?
05:16 Jordan: yes we can meet that if legal turnaround is fast — we'll aim to have redlines and SOW by 4/18.
05:22 Priya: technical acceptance criteria: let's define a test set and availability windows. I propose three items: 1) endpoint correctness (sample prompts pass), 2) latency under 95th percentile target for a defined prompt mix, 3) data handling verification via audit logs.
05:37 Ravi: we also need load test results — can Redwood run a 75M token simulated month or give a benchmark equivalent?
05:45 Priya: we can run a scaled load test on a mirror infra and provide results and a KV cache hit-rate profile. That will show cost projection.
05:53 Nora: again, please include cost sensitivity — if cache hit drops to 60% what's the delta?
05:59 Priya: yes we'll show cache hit sensitivity and how batching impacts unit cost.
06:07 Amanda: on SSO — we need SAML support and SCIM provisioning, tether to Okta. any gotchas?
06:14 Liam: we support SAML and SCIM; for Okta we have a template. There is a short window for provisioning/SSO testing which usually takes 48 hours.
06:23 Tom: audit rights — enterprise needs a window for on-prem audits or remote audit support. What's Redwood's stance?
06:30 Jordan: we allow remote audits against SOC 2 plus a cooperative on-site audit under NDA and reasonable notice. We'll add audit-rig language.
06:39 Ravi: incident process — 15 minute ack window for SEV1? that seems aggressive. what's your practice?
06:46 Priya: we do an immediate page for SEV1 and a 15-minute ack internal target, external communication within 30 minutes for critical incidents. We can adjust timelines contractually if required.
06:59 Tom: also want a named escalation contact and a runbook excerpt in the contract appendix.
07:06 Jordan: we'll include primary on-call and escalation ladder.
07:12 Amanda: anything else on DPA—data residency clause needs to say EU data remains in EU unless we authorize export.
07:20 Priya: yes, we can support region tenancy and ensure keys for EU are deployed in EU regional KMS. Fallback would still respect data residency but operational steps require approval.
07:34 Nora: quick clarification: pilot billing — are invoices monthly in arrears or prepaid?
07:39 Jordan: invoicing is monthly in arrears for hosted; for dedicated we request a monthly minimum or prepay option. We'll document both.
07:48 Amanda: ok good. next steps recap?
07:52 Jordan: recap — Jordan will circulate redlined MSA + DPA and pilot SOW by 4/18; Priya will send KMS BYOK diagram and load-test plan by 4/16; Liam will attach SCIM/SAML template; customer to provide estimated token volumes by 4/18.
08:10 Tom: we'll review redlines and try to get legal signoff by 4/28.
08:15 Amanda: procurement will review pricing worksheet when received; Nora will sign off on the modeled scenarios.
08:21 Ravi: we'll set up a follow-up technical runbook call — week of 4/21.
08:26 Jordan: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll share links: pilot SOW template (link: https://redwood.example/pilot-sow), MSA clean copy and current sub-processor list.
08:39 Amanda: thanks all.
